faqs.question: What is JSON formatting?
faqs.answer: JSON formatting (pretty-printing) adds consistent indentation and newlines to make JSON human-readable. Minified JSON is identical in data content but has all whitespace removed to reduce file size.

faqs.question: Does this formatter change my data?
faqs.answer: No. Formatting only adds whitespace characters. All keys, values, order, and structure are preserved exactly. You can safely format and re-minify without any data loss.

faqs.question: Can I format invalid JSON?
faqs.answer: No. JSON must be syntactically valid before it can be formatted. If your JSON is broken, use the JSON Repair tool first, then format the fixed output.

faqs.question: What is the maximum JSON size I can format?
faqs.answer: The formatter runs entirely in your browser. In practice it handles JSON up to tens of megabytes on modern devices. Very large files may cause a brief delay while the browser processes the text.

faqs.question: Is there a difference between JSON Formatter and JSON Beautifier?
faqs.answer: They do the same thing: add indentation to make JSON readable. The Beautifier tool on this site provides the same core functionality with a slightly different interface layout.

faqs.question: Is the JSON formatter free? Do I need an account?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's completely free with no account, no sign-up, and no usage limits. Your JSON is processed entirely in your browser, so nothing is ever uploaded or stored.

faqs.question: What does 'beautify' mean for JSON?
faqs.answer: Beautifying JSON means adding consistent indentation, line breaks, and spacing so the structure is easy to read at a glance. It is the opposite of minification, which removes all such whitespace.

faqs.question: Does beautifying affect JSON parsing?
faqs.answer: No. A JSON parser treats whitespace as insignificant. A beautified and a minified version of the same JSON are semantically identical and parse to the same data structure.

faqs.question: Can I paste JSON from a browser network tab?
faqs.answer: Yes. JSON copied directly from browser DevTools network responses is often compact or partially formatted. Paste it here and it becomes fully readable immediately.

faqs.question: Does it work with JSON arrays?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both JSON objects (curly braces) and JSON arrays (square brackets) are formatted correctly, including deeply nested combinations of both.

faqs.question: What makes JSON invalid?
faqs.answer: Common causes include: trailing commas after the last item in an object or array, single-quoted strings instead of double-quoted, unquoted keys, missing commas between items, incorrect nesting of brackets or braces, and unescaped control characters in strings.

faqs.question: Does this validator support JSON5 or JSONC?
faqs.answer: No. This tool validates strict JSON per RFC 8259. JSON5 (which allows comments and trailing commas) and JSONC (JSON with Comments) are not valid JSON. Use JSON Repair to strip those extensions and produce valid JSON.

faqs.question: Can I validate a JSON Schema file?
faqs.answer: A JSON Schema file is just a JSON document. The JSON Validator checks that it is syntactically valid JSON. To validate the schema itself against the JSON Schema specification, use the JSON Schema Validator tool.

faqs.answer: The validator runs in your browser with no upload. You can validate JSON files of any size, though very large files may take a moment to process.

faqs.question: Why does my JSON show as invalid when it looks correct?
faqs.answer: Check for: a trailing comma after the last property in an object or array, a key without quotes, a value using undefined or a JavaScript function, or a BOM (byte order mark) at the start of the text. Copy the error line number to find the exact issue.

faqs.question: What does JSON minification do?
faqs.answer: Minification removes all whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, newlines) that are not inside string values. The resulting JSON is identical in data content but takes up less space, which reduces network payload size and parse time.

faqs.question: How much smaller does minified JSON get?
faqs.answer: Depending on how heavily indented the original is, minification typically reduces JSON size by 20-40%. For deeply nested objects with 4-space indentation, savings can reach 50%.

faqs.question: Does minification remove comments?
faqs.answer: Standard JSON does not allow comments, so a valid JSON file will not have any. If your JSON has comments (JSONC style), they must be stripped first using JSON Repair before minifying.

faqs.question: Will minified JSON still parse correctly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every JSON parser correctly handles minified JSON. Whitespace outside of string values is always optional in the JSON specification.

faqs.question: What is a JSON tree viewer?
faqs.answer: A JSON tree viewer renders JSON as a hierarchical tree of expandable nodes, similar to the view you see in browser DevTools. It makes deeply nested structures much easier to navigate than reading raw text.

faqs.question: Can I edit values in the viewer?
faqs.answer: The viewer is read-only for exploration. To edit JSON, use the JSON Editor tool which provides a side-by-side tree editor and text input.

faqs.question: Does it work with very large JSON files?
faqs.answer: The viewer loads the entire JSON into the browser. For very large files (over a few MB), rendering all nodes at once may be slow. Collapsing top-level nodes first and then expanding what you need is the most efficient approach.

faqs.question: Are circular references supported?
faqs.answer: Circular references are not valid JSON (JSON must be serialisable), so any valid JSON file will not contain them. The viewer handles all valid JSON structures.

faqs.question: What types of JSON errors can be repaired?
faqs.answer: JSON Repair handles: trailing commas after the last item in objects or arrays, single-quoted strings (converts to double-quoted), unquoted object keys (adds double quotes), missing commas between items (attempts to insert them), stray quotes, and some truncated JSON structures.

faqs.question: Can it repair completely garbled JSON?
faqs.answer: The repair tool works best on JSON that has common human or tool-introduced errors. Fundamentally garbled or corrupted text (such as binary data labelled as JSON) cannot be repaired, as there is no correct structure to recover.

faqs.question: Does repair change my data values?
faqs.answer: No. Repair only fixes structural and syntax issues - punctuation, quote types, and bracket matching. Your key names, string values, numbers, and booleans are not modified.

faqs.answer: JSON Repair can handle several JS-style patterns (unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing commas) that are common when copying from JS source files. Full JSON5 with comments is also handled by stripping comment lines.

faqs.question: What is JSONL (JSON Lines)?
faqs.answer: JSONL (also called NDJSON - Newline Delimited JSON) is a format where each line of a file contains a complete, independent JSON value. It is popular for log files, data streaming, and large datasets because each line can be read and parsed independently without loading the whole file.

faqs.question: Is JSONL the same as a JSON array?
faqs.answer: No. A JSON array is a single JSON document containing multiple values in brackets. JSONL is a sequence of completely separate JSON values, one per line, with no surrounding brackets.

faqs.question: Can I format only some lines?
faqs.answer: The formatter processes every line. If some lines are invalid JSON they are passed through unchanged (or flagged, depending on the setting). Valid lines are always formatted.

faqs.question: What happens with empty lines in the input?
faqs.answer: Empty lines are preserved in the output. Lines containing only whitespace are treated as blank and skipped during formatting.

faqs.question: How is JSONL validation different from JSON validation?
faqs.answer: A JSON validator checks one document at a time. A JSONL validator checks each line of the file as an independent JSON document. A single invalid line does not invalidate the rest of the file.

faqs.question: What counts as a valid JSONL line?
faqs.answer: Any complete, valid JSON value on a single line: an object, array, string, number, boolean, or null. The line must be syntactically complete - partial JSON is not valid in JSONL format.

faqs.question: Are blank lines allowed in JSONL?
faqs.answer: Blank lines are technically not part of the JSONL specification but most parsers skip them. The validator ignores blank lines and only checks non-empty lines.

faqs.question: Can I use this to validate log files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Application logs in JSONL format can be pasted directly. The validator identifies which log lines have malformed JSON, which is useful for debugging logging pipelines.

faqs.question: Does JSON Diff care about key order?
faqs.answer: No. JSON objects are unordered by definition. The diff compares values by key name, not position. Reordered keys with identical values show no difference.

faqs.question: Does it diff nested objects and arrays?
faqs.answer: Yes. The diff is recursive and descends into nested objects and arrays. Changes deep in the structure are highlighted exactly where they occur.

faqs.question: What does the diff show for array changes?
faqs.answer: Array items are compared positionally - item 0 is compared with item 0, item 1 with item 1, etc. If an item is inserted or removed, all subsequent items will show as changed. For semantic array diffs, key-based comparison on an object property may be more useful.

faqs.question: Can I diff API responses?
faqs.answer: Yes. Copy a JSON response from your browser DevTools Network tab and paste it into each panel. This is a common use case for verifying that a code change did not unexpectedly alter an API response.

faqs.question: Is there a size limit?
faqs.answer: The diff runs entirely in your browser. Large JSON files work but may take a few seconds for the diffing algorithm to complete. For very large files (over a few MB), consider diffing a representative sample first.

faqs.question: Why would I sort JSON keys?
faqs.answer: Sorted keys make JSON easier to scan visually, simplify manual comparison between documents, and produce consistent output for version control diffs - two JSON objects with the same data but different key order will show as identical in a diff after sorting.

faqs.question: Does sorting change the data?
faqs.answer: No. JSON object keys are semantically unordered, so reordering them does not change what the JSON represents. All values remain associated with their correct keys.

faqs.question: Are arrays sorted?
faqs.answer: Array items are not sorted - their order is meaningful and preserved. Only object keys (property names) are alphabetically reordered. If you need array items sorted, that requires a more specialised tool.

faqs.question: Does it sort nested objects too?
faqs.answer: Yes. The sort is applied recursively throughout the entire document, including objects nested inside arrays or other objects.

faqs.question: What is a deep merge?
faqs.answer: A deep merge combines two objects recursively. When both objects share a key that contains another object, the nested objects are merged too rather than one replacing the other. A shallow merge would simply overwrite the nested object entirely.

faqs.question: What happens when both objects have the same key?
faqs.answer: The second object's value wins. If both values are objects, they are recursively merged. If either value is a primitive, array, or null, the second value replaces the first.

faqs.question: How are arrays merged?
faqs.answer: Arrays are replaced, not merged element-by-element. If both objects have the same key containing an array, the second object's array completely replaces the first. Array concatenation is not performed automatically.

faqs.question: Can I merge more than two objects?
faqs.answer: The tool merges two objects at a time. To merge three or more objects, merge the first two, then paste the result as the base and merge with the third object.

faqs.question: What does flattening JSON mean?
faqs.answer: Flattening converts nested JSON like {"a":{"b":{"c":1}}} into a flat object with dot-path keys like {"a.b.c":1}. Every value in the original, no matter how deeply nested, becomes a key at the top level with its full path as the key name.

faqs.question: What is unflattening?
faqs.answer: Unflattening is the reverse: it takes a flat object with dot-path keys and rebuilds the nested structure. It is the inverse operation of flattening.

faqs.question: What separator is used in the flattened keys?
faqs.answer: By default the tool uses a dot (.) as the separator, producing keys like user.address.city. Some variants use forward slashes or underscores. The separator can be configured in the tool options.

faqs.question: How are arrays handled during flattening?
faqs.answer: Array indices become part of the path. For example, {"items":[{"id":1}]} flattens to {"items.0.id":1}. Unflattening correctly reconstructs arrays from numeric indices in the path.

faqs.question: What is JSONPath?
faqs.answer: JSONPath is a query language for JSON, analogous to XPath for XML. It lets you navigate and extract values from JSON using path expressions. It is widely used in APIs, testing tools, and configuration systems.

faqs.question: What JSONPath syntax is supported?
faqs.answer: This tool supports the standard JSONPath operators: $ (root), . (child), .. (recursive descent), * (wildcard), [n] (array index), [start:end] (slice), [?(expression)] (filter), and @ (current node in filter).

faqs.question: What does $..price return?
faqs.answer: The .. operator is the recursive descent operator. $..price returns all values with the key 'price' anywhere in the document, regardless of depth.

faqs.question: Can I use filter expressions?
faqs.answer: Yes. Filter expressions use the [?(@.property operator value)] syntax. For example, $.books[?(@.price < 20)] returns all book objects where price is less than 20.

faqs.question: Are results shown as a JSON array?
faqs.answer: Yes. The results panel shows matching values as a JSON array. If a single value matches, it appears as a one-element array. If no values match, an empty array is returned.

faqs.question: Can I convert a single JSON object instead of an array?

faqs.question: What is Base64?
faqs.answer: Base64 is a binary-to-text encoding scheme that represents binary data using a set of 64 printable ASCII characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, +, /). It is used to encode binary data (like images or files) into text form so it can be safely transmitted in text-based systems like email, HTML, or JSON.

faqs.question: Is Base64 encryption?
faqs.answer: No. Base64 is encoding, not encryption. It is fully reversible by anyone without a key. Never use Base64 to protect sensitive data - use a proper encryption algorithm instead.

faqs.question: What is URL-safe Base64?
faqs.answer: Standard Base64 uses + and / characters which have special meaning in URLs. URL-safe Base64 replaces + with - and / with _, making the encoded string safe to include in URLs without percent-encoding.

faqs.question: Why does Base64 output end with = or ==?
faqs.answer: Base64 encodes data in 3-byte groups. If the input length is not a multiple of 3, padding characters (=) are added to make the last group complete. One = means one padding byte was added; == means two.

faqs.answer: The decoder runs entirely in your browser - your JWT is never sent anywhere. However, treat JWTs as sensitive tokens and avoid pasting production tokens with long lifetimes into any online tool.

faqs.question: Does the decoder verify the JWT signature?
faqs.answer: No. The decoder only decodes the Base64url-encoded header and payload. It does not verify the signature, which requires the signing secret or public key. Use this tool for inspection only, not for security validation.

faqs.question: What are JWT claims?
faqs.answer: Claims are key-value pairs in the JWT payload. Standard claims include: iss (issuer), sub (subject), aud (audience), exp (expiry time), nbf (not before), iat (issued at), and jti (JWT ID). Custom claims are any additional properties added by the issuing application.

faqs.question: What algorithms does the header alg field refer to?
faqs.answer: Common values: HS256 (HMAC-SHA256, symmetric), RS256 (RSA-SHA256, asymmetric), ES256 (ECDSA-SHA256, asymmetric). HS256 uses a shared secret; RS256 and ES256 use a public/private key pair.

faqs.question: Why is my token showing as invalid?

faqs.question: Why does token count matter for LLMs?
faqs.answer: LLM APIs charge per token and have a maximum context window. Knowing the token count of your JSON payload helps you stay within limits, estimate costs, and avoid hitting context window errors in production.

faqs.question: What is a token?
faqs.answer: A token is the basic unit that LLMs process. Tokens are not the same as words or characters - they are variable-length text chunks determined by the model's tokeniser. Common English words are usually one token; long words, JSON syntax, and non-English characters may be multiple tokens.

faqs.question: How accurate is the estimate?

faqs.question: Does minifying JSON reduce token count?
faqs.answer: Yes. Minifying removes whitespace, which means fewer characters and therefore fewer tokens. For large JSON payloads, minifying can reduce token count by 15-30%.

faqs.question: What's the difference between camelCase and PascalCase?

faqs.question: How does Title Case handle small words?

faqs.question: What do aLtErNaTiNg and InVeRsE do?
faqs.answer: aLtErNaTiNg alternates lowercase/uppercase per letter for that mocking-spongebob meme style. InVeRsE flips the case of every letter: 'Hello' becomes 'hELLO' - handy for fixing text typed with Caps Lock on.

faqs.answer: In practice, no. With 122 random bits you'd need to generate about a billion UUIDs per second for 85 years to reach a 50% collision chance. For IDs, v4 is effectively unique.

faqs.question: Should I use UUIDs as database primary keys?
faqs.answer: They work, but random UUIDs fragment indexes in some databases. If you need sortable IDs, consider UUIDv7 (time-ordered) - this tool generates v4, which is best for tokens, request IDs and test data.

faqs.question: What's the difference between UUID and GUID?

faqs.question: What is the Pomodoro Technique?

faqs.question: Where are my tasks stored?
faqs.answer: In your browser's local storage, on your device only. They are never uploaded anywhere, so they persist between visits on the same browser but cannot follow you to another device.
